claims.text: There is a significant positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
In-situ TEM or XRD can provide real-time information about microstructure and phase evolution during processing.
Using in-situ characterization can facilitate development of a method that enables large-scale reaction and a stable microstructure in RHEA–Cu systems.
Real-time monitoring of microstructure and phase evolution enables optimization of processing conditions.
Real-time monitoring of microstructure and phase evolution enables optimization of alloy composition.
The proposed use of in-situ characterization will improve the mechanical properties of RHEA–Cu materials.
The proposed use of in-situ characterization will produce a stable microstructure in RHEA–Cu materials.
Conventional methods for forming RHEA–Cu composite structures result in unstable microstructures.
In-situ characterization techniques have resolution limitations.
In-situ characterization techniques have sampling limitations.
Factors other than the monitored phase and microstructure evolution may influence the microstructure and properties of RHEA–Cu materials.
